items.claim: A hunter can break anti-forgery defences without ever forging a token value, by changing the request shape itself: switching the request method POST to GET, dropping the token parameter, blanking it, replaying an unused valid token, feeding the victim the attacker's own token, matching only the token's length, mutating one character, or switching Content-Type to a multipart form instead of json/x-www-form-urlencoded.
items.body:
A hunter can break anti-forgery defences without ever forging a token value, by changing the request shape itself: switching the request method POST to GET, dropping the token parameter, blanking it, replaying an unused valid token, feeding the victim the attacker's own token, matching only the token's length, mutating one character, or switching Content-Type to a multipart form instead of json/x-www-form-urlencoded.

HackTricks reference: cross site request forgery bypass (https://kathan19.gitbook.io/howtohunt/csrf/cross_site_request_forgery_bypass.md)
items.disproof: If the endpoint rejects every one of those mutations (method switch, removed/blanked/altered token, replayed or attacker-supplied token, Content-Type change, stripped referer) with the same consistent rejection, the anti-forgery control is holding.

items.claim: A cross-site request forgery finding is only actionable if the target exposes a relevant state-changing action; without one there is nothing to forge and the report does not stand.

If the 'None' value is used, a website may create a cross-domain POST HTTP request to another website, and the browser automatically adds cookies to this request. This may lead to Cross-Site-Request-Forgery (CSRF) attacks if there are no additional protections in place (such as Anti-CSRF tokens).

items.claim: A cross-site request forgery proof-of-concept can be a standalone auto-submitting HTML form placed on an attacker page, so the evidence reproduces with no session scripting and shows the forged request originates cross-origin.

items.disproof: Opening the generated auto-submit page from an origin the target does not trust produces no state change in the victim account, so the page proves nothing.
